faqs.answer: No. The letters are pixels inside the SVG, not paths or text drawn from fonts, so enlarging the SVG does not redraw them any sharper.

faqs.question: How are long lines wrapped?
faqs.answer: Lines break between words once they reach the picture's fixed width. A word too long for a line is broken inside the word.

faqs.question: Is there a limit on how much text fits?
faqs.answer: Yes. Beyond a fixed number of lines the text is cut off, the final line names the line where it stopped, and the page tells you it was cut.

faqs.question: Why do my accented letters look wrong?
faqs.answer: The page reads the file as UTF-8, or as UTF-16 when it starts with a byte order mark, and otherwise as Windows-1252. A file saved in another encoding shows the wrong characters, so save it as UTF-8 and try again.

faqs.question: Which font and colors does the picture use?
faqs.answer: Black letters on white, set in DejaVu Sans with a margin around the text. Scripts that font lacks, such as Chinese or emoji, fall back to your browser's sans-serif font.

faqs.question: Does it handle Hebrew and Arabic?
faqs.answer: Yes. When a line begins with a Hebrew or Arabic letter, it is drawn from right to left, and DejaVu Sans covers both scripts.

faqs.question: What happens to tabs and terminal colors?
faqs.answer: Tabs stop every 4 characters. Other control characters and terminal color codes are dropped, so only the readable text is drawn.

guide.title: TXT files and SVG output
guide.markdown:
### What is a TXT file?

Plain text is what a TXT file holds: characters with no fonts, styles or images. Any text editor opens it, which is why it turns up as notes, logs, readme files and configuration. It has no page layout either, so turning it into a graphic means choosing a font, a width and margins.

The one thing a TXT file does carry is a character encoding such as UTF-8. A receiving program reads the bytes through that encoding, so the same file can show correct text in one program and wrong characters in another.

### Programs that open TXT files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- Visual Studio Code opens and edits text files.
- Vim edits plain text.

**Mac:**

- TextEdit works on plain text files. Converting rich text to plain text there removes its styles and formatting.

### TXT and SVG compared

A TXT file is text/plain, with no layout of its own. An SVG is XML with the type image/svg+xml, and it can describe shapes, text and embedded pixel images.

This page uses the embedded picture. It draws your text on a canvas in DejaVu Sans, black on white, at 16 px on 24 px lines with 32 px margins, wrapped at 800 px, and wraps the resulting PNG in an SVG. The SVG holds no text and no paths, so its words cannot be selected or searched.

### Other ways to convert TXT to SVG

- **LibreOffice Draw:** click the page, choose Insert > File, select the TXT and click Insert, then click OK in the Insert Text dialog. Choose File > Export, select SVG as the file type and save. SVG shows no options dialog on export.
- **ImageMagick with Inkscape:** run `magick -size 800x -pointsize 16 caption:@note.txt note.png` to draw the text file as a PNG. Import the PNG into Inkscape with File > Import, choose the embed option and save the result as SVG. This also gives pixels, not text.

### Problems with TXT files

- **Strange characters**: the encoding was guessed wrongly. Save the file as UTF-8.
- **Formatting disappeared**: plain text never held any. A TXT file keeps no formatting from a styled document.
- **An image or table is missing**: a plain text file has no place to hold a picture or a table.

guide.title: VOB files and MOV output
guide.markdown:
### What is a VOB file?

VOB is the DVD Video Object. A DVD-Video disc keeps its video, sound, text overlays and menus inside VOB streams, which are based on the MPEG-2 program stream. A disc copy usually puts them in a VIDEO_TS folder next to companion IFO and BUP files, and a loose VOB does not replace that structure. A VOB file on a disc is limited to 1 GB, so a long film is split across several of them. People meet VOB files when ripping DVDs to files, and a disc can hold several titles, so choosing the wrong one gives the wrong clip.

### Programs that open VOB files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- VLC media player reads DVD-Video media and MPEG program streams.
- HandBrake accepts VOB files as well as complete VIDEO_TS disc folders. Its input must be unprotected.

### VOB and MOV compared

A VOB is a DVD container with several audio and text-overlay streams, and some discs are encrypted with CSS. A MOV is Apple's QuickTime container, registered as video/quicktime, with the extension .mov or .qt. It holds video, audio, text and timecode tracks, and many codecs including H.264 and ProRes. The QuickTime format was the basis for the MPEG-4 file format, but MOV and MP4 are separate formats.

This page decodes the VOB and writes new H.264 video and AAC sound into a MOV, so it is not a copy of the DVD streams. Frames flagged as interlaced are deinterlaced. The picture may be 1920 px on its longer side at most, and the frame rate may be 30 fps at most.

### Other ways to convert VOB to MOV

- **FFmpeg, H.264 and AAC:** run `ffmpeg -i scene.vob -c:a aac -b:a 192k -c:v libx264 -crf 21 scene.mov` to re-encode both streams.
- **FFmpeg, stream copy:** run `ffmpeg -i scene.vob -c copy scene-copy.mov`. Stream copy passes the packets through without decoding or encoding.
- **FFmpeg, ProRes:** run `ffmpeg -i scene.vob -c:v prores_ks scene-edit.mov` to encode the video as ProRes, one of the codecs a MOV can hold.

### Problems with VOB files

- **The clip is too short**: you chose one segment, or the wrong title on a disc with several.
- **No menus**: they are part of the DVD structure, which a loose VOB lacks.
- **Overlays missing**: a player that plays MPEG-2 video can still skip the DVD text overlays, which can be bitmap images rather than text.
- **A protected disc fails**: HandBrake does not process copy-protected DVD sources.

guide.title: WAV files and OPUS output
guide.markdown:
### What is a WAV file?

The Waveform Audio File Format (WAV) wraps sound in RIFF chunks and was documented by Microsoft and IBM in 1991. It usually holds uncompressed linear PCM, so files are large but exact. Compressed encodings can appear inside too. Broadcast WAVE extends it with production metadata, and the Library of Congress also recommends WAV for digital audio collections. People use it for recording, editing and professional sound production.

### Programs that open WAV files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- Audacity brings in most WAV files, all PCM variants included.
- ffplay plays WAV, using the demuxer FFmpeg includes for it.

**Mobile:**

- Firefox for Android lists WAV among its supported audio types.
- VLC for Android is a free mobile media player.
- mpv for Android is the Android port linked by the mpv project.

### WAV and Opus compared

WAV is audio/wav or audio/x-wav and usually lossless, with a 4 GB file size limit. Opus is an open lossy codec from the IETF, defined in RFC 6716, which combines Skype's SILK and Xiph.Org's CELT. Ogg Opus supports descriptive metadata and seeking. Opus bitrates run from 6 to 510 kbit/s, it has low latency and it is royalty-free.

Here FFmpeg in your browser runs libopus on the WAV's sound with a 128 kbps target and compression level 4. Any picture stream is dropped. Nothing in the page lets you change the sample rate, channels or tags.

### Other ways to convert WAV to Opus

- **opusenc:** run `opusenc --bitrate 128 take.wav take.opus` from the opus-tools. It reads Wave input and writes Ogg Opus, with the bitrate in kbit/s.
- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i take.wav -c:a libopus -b:a 128k take.opus`. The libopus encoder is a wrapper that requires --enable-libopus.
- **Audacity:** choose File > Import > Audio and select the WAV. Then choose File > Export Audio, pick Opus as the format, name the file and export.

### Problems with WAV files

- **A recorder's WAV won't import**: it may use proprietary compression. Audacity recommends its FFmpeg library for such files.
- **Very large recordings**: they may need RF64 instead of the original size fields.
- **Tags differ**: INFO chunks and Broadcast WAVE store different information.

guide.title: WMA files and M4A output
guide.markdown:
### What is a WMA file?

Microsoft's Windows Media Audio is a family of codecs, kept in the ASF container. The .wma extension separates audio-only files from other ASF content. Variants include standard, Professional, Lossless and Voice, and WMA 9 supports variable bit rate. The usual media type is audio/x-ms-wma. People use it for delivering music and sometimes for intermediate audio storage.

### Programs that open WMA files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- VLC media player supports ASF/WMA input and carries multiple Windows Media Audio decoders.
- Audacity can read unprotected WMA, provided the optional FFmpeg library is added.
- FFmpeg's support matrix covers decoding the WMA 1 and WMA 2 codecs, as well as Pro, Voice and Lossless.

**Windows:**

- Adobe Audition imports WMA only with DLMS Format Support switched on.

### WMA and M4A compared

WMA is a codec family, lossy except for the Lossless variant. Apple adopted the M4A extension, used for MPEG-4 files with audio only, for its unprotected music files. Most M4A files contain AAC, a lossy codec defined in MPEG-4 Part 3 that aims for better sound than MP3 at a comparable bitrate. Apple used it for songs sold through iTunes. The media type is audio/mp4. Android plays AAC in .m4a files, and the major browsers play AAC inside MP4.

This page decodes the WMA and encodes AAC at 192 kbps with FFmpeg in your browser. Picture streams are left out.

### Other ways to convert WMA to M4A

- **FFmpeg, AAC:** run `ffmpeg -i library.wma -vn -c:a aac -b:a 192k listening.m4a`. The `-vn` flag drops video streams, and the output is encoded afresh with loss.
- **Audacity:** with the optional FFmpeg library installed, open the WMA and use File > Export Audio with the M4A(AAC) Files FFmpeg format.

### Problems with WMA files

- **Audacity can't import it**: the optional FFmpeg library is missing, or the file is protected.
- **One program plays it, another doesn't**: an application may decode one WMA codec yet fail on another, because the .wma name does not reveal the variant inside.
- **A protected file**: Audacity cannot import protected WMA through its FFmpeg library.
- **Check the result**: play the M4A before deleting the WMA, since AAC discards detail from the decoded sound.

guide.title: WPG files and JPG output
guide.markdown:
### What is a WPG file?

WPG means WordPerfect Graphics, the graphics format of the WordPerfect word processor. It belongs to the WordPerfect graphics family and was used for clip art and legacy office graphics. Its files may hold vector drawing objects, bitmap data or both, and Corel describes a palette of up to 256 selected colors. Corel separates version 1.0, which targets WordPerfect 5.1 and earlier, from version 2.0, which targets WordPerfect 6 and newer.

### Programs that open WPG files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- ImageMagick can read WPG images.
- XnView MP reads WPG too, and private or educational use costs nothing.

**Windows:**

- CorelDRAW imports WPG drawings through File > Import.
- Corel PHOTO-PAINT can open a WPG as a new image or bring it into one that is already open.

### WPG and JPG compared

A WPG may be vector or raster. A JPG is a lossy raster format for photographs, defined by ISO/IEC 10918-1, with no alpha channel, and .jpg and .jpeg are the same format. Any vector structure is lost in the move to JPG.

Here ImageMagick, running in your browser, reads one image from the WPG and writes the JPG. Only the bitmap records are drawn, and vector records are skipped. The page passes no quality setting. Beyond roughly 537 megapixels the picture is declined as too big. A batch gives one JPG per WPG.

### Other ways to convert WPG to JPG

- **CorelDRAW:** choose File > Import, select the WPG file type, click Import and click the page to place it. Then choose File > Export, pick JPG in the Save as type list and click Export. Corel lists limitations for WPG import.
- **LibreOffice Draw:** open the WPG, which Draw lists among its graphics formats, then choose File > Export and pick JPEG.
- **ImageMagick:** run `magick illustration.wpg illustration.jpg`. ImageMagick lists WPG as a format it reads.

### Problems with WPG files

- **Elements missing after import**: CorelDRAW keeps embedded WMF and EMF graphics but can discard other embedded elements, and it documents that Graphics Text Type 2 is not supported.
- **Wrong version**: WPG 2.0 is not suitable when the destination needs WordPerfect 5.1 compatibility.
- **This page can't convert the drawing**: it was made only of vector objects, which the reader here skips. Export from CorelDRAW or LibreOffice Draw instead.

guide.title: XCF files and SVG output
guide.markdown:
### What is an XCF file?

GIMP, the GNU Image Manipulation Program, saves its working images as XCF. It keeps layers, channels, paths and selections so an image can be edited again, and it retains transparency rather than only a flattened picture. The undo history is not saved. GIMP's Save writes XCF, while other formats go through Export, and GIMP does not position XCF as an interchange format.

### Programs that open XCF files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- GIMP is the native project editor and preserves the working image when saved as XCF.
- ImageMagick reads XCF, though you should not assume third-party rendering reproduces every GIMP feature.

### XCF and SVG compared

An XCF is a layered, lossless working file. An SVG is an XML vector format with the type image/svg+xml, though it can also embed pixel images.

This page reads one picture from the XCF with ImageMagick and embeds it in an SVG as a PNG, so no paths are created and nothing in the SVG can be edited as a shape. Layers are not written out one by one. The page turns away anything above about 537 megapixels. A batch of XCF files is processed in turn, one SVG per file.

### Other ways to convert XCF to SVG

- **GIMP path export:** open the XCF in GIMP, choose Windows > Dockable Dialogs > Paths, right-click the path you want and pick Export Paths, then save the file. GIMP saves the path in SVG format.
- **GIMP and Inkscape wrapper:** in GIMP choose File > Export As and export a PNG. Open Inkscape, bring the PNG in through File > Import with embed selected, and save it as SVG. The result keeps pixels instead of vector shapes.
- **GIMP and Inkscape tracing:** export the picture as PNG in GIMP and import it into Inkscape. With the Selector tool on the image, open Path > Trace Bitmap, adjust the options, preview with Update and accept with Ok. Expect the trace to differ from the original.

### Problems with XCF files

- **A viewer can't open it**: most ordinary image viewers cannot read XCF, so export a display copy from GIMP.
- **Flattened exports lose layers**: a flattened export cannot carry every project property, so the XCF is the file to edit later.
- **A save warning after export**: an export leaves the XCF itself unsaved, so GIMP may still ask about saving on close.
- **Rendering differs from GIMP**: another program that reads XCF may not reproduce every GIMP feature.

faqs.question: Will the FLAC sound better than the AAC?
faqs.answer: No. FLAC keeps every sample it is given, but the AAC had already lost detail, and converting cannot recreate it.

faqs.question: Why is the FLAC bigger than the AAC?
faqs.answer: The AAC was compressed with loss, and FLAC stores the decoded audio without loss, so the file can be much larger.

faqs.question: Can I choose a FLAC compression level?

guide.title: AAC files and FLAC output
guide.markdown:
### What is an AAC file?

Advanced Audio Coding, or AAC, is a lossy, perceptual audio coding family standardized through MPEG. It is specified in MPEG-2 Part 7 and placed in MPEG-4 Part 3. AAC can sit in MP4, QuickTime or other wrappers, and a standalone .aac file commonly carries ADTS framing. The media type audio/aac covers ADTS and LATM/LOAS transport. LC, HE-AAC and HE-AAC v2 are among its profiles, and it serves streaming and delivery to listeners.

### Programs that open AAC files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- VLC media player reads raw AAC files and decodes MPEG-4 AAC.
- FFmpeg decodes AAC and also has its own AAC encoder.

**Windows and Mac:**

- Adobe Audition imports AAC, including HE-AAC.

### AAC and FLAC compared

FLAC squeezes integer PCM audio and throws no samples away. It supports one through eight channels, carries metadata such as seek points, pictures and Vorbis comments, and uses the audio/flac media type. RFC 9639 standardized its description in December 2024. FLAC is an open, royalty-free codec developed by Xiph.Org, and people use it for music archiving, audiophile listening and lossless backups of CDs.

This page decodes the AAC and writes FLAC with FFmpeg in your browser, without a picture stream. The FLAC is lossless only from the point of decoding. The page has no settings, and a batch yields one FLAC per AAC.

### Other ways to convert AAC to FLAC

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i speech.aac -vn -c:a flac speech-decoded.flac`. With `-vn` no video stream is written, and `-c:a flac` picks the FLAC encoder.
- **VLC:** choose Media > Convert/Save, add the AAC, click Convert, pick the Audio - FLAC profile, set a .flac destination and click Start.

### Problems with AAC files

- **The sound is not as good as hoped**: a lossy AAC already lost detail, and changing it to FLAC cannot recreate the samples that were removed.
- **A decoder rejects it**: an MPEG-2 AAC decoder may not follow the MPEG-4 variants.
- **Renaming did nothing**: giving the file an .m4a name leaves the ADTS framing as it was; no MP4 wrapper appears.
- **The decoded file is much larger**: once decoded, the audio can need far more space than the compressed original did.

guide.title: AI files and TIFF output
guide.markdown:
### What is an AI file?

AI is Adobe Illustrator's native artwork format. Inside it sit vector paths, shapes, text and effects arranged in layers and artboards, and pixel images can sit among the vector objects. Illustrator 9 changed the format in 2000, and earlier files used PostScript. This page reads the PDF rendition that the PDF-compatible saving option stores next to the Illustrator data. Logos, illustrations and print layouts are typical AI source files.

### Programs that open AI files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- ImageMagick reads AI as Illustrator CS2. That is rendering, not Illustrator editing.

**Windows and Mac:**

- Adobe Illustrator opens native artwork with its editable objects.

**Linux:**

- Inkscape imports AI artwork from Illustrator 9.0 onward, and some document features may be unavailable.

### AI and TIFF compared

TIFF is a tag-based raster wrapper developed by Aldus and Microsoft. Revision 6.0 appeared in 1992, and Adobe now controls the specification. Compression methods and color representations vary between TIFFs, and one file can hold several images, as in a scanned page sequence. Its extensions are .tif and .tiff, with the media type image/tiff.

Here PDF.js draws each page of the PDF inside the AI, and the pixels are written as a TIFF on an opaque white background. Each page is drawn at up to double its size, and a very large artboard is scaled down to stay within a pixel budget of about 16.8 megapixels. Every page is a separate file with no ZIP, named name_page1, name_page2 and so on. You can choose several AI files at once, and they run one after another. The page sets no print resolution, so artwork meant for a printer's dpi spec should be exported from Illustrator. A file with no PDF inside fails with a message telling you to resave it with Create PDF Compatible File turned on.

### Other ways to convert AI to TIFF

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick -density 300 artwork.ai artwork.tiff`. The -density option sets the canvas resolution used when a vector format is rendered to a raster image.

### Problems with AI files

- **No PDF inside**: other software can fail on an AI that lacks its PDF-compatible representation. Resave it from Illustrator with that option on.
- **Not editable afterwards**: reading the embedded PDF gives no native Illustrator objects, so the AI stays your editable master.
- **Missing links**: a linked image stays outside the file unless Include Linked Files was ticked when saving, so the TIFF can lack it.
- **Older Illustrator versions**: opening artwork in an older version can cause compatibility problems, so match or exceed the saving version.
- **Blurry when enlarged**: the TIFF is pixels, so render again at the size you need.
- **Layers are gone**: the TIFF is flattened.

guide.title: AIFF files and M4A output
guide.markdown:
### What is an AIFF file?

Apple developed the Audio Interchange File Format in 1988 on top of the IFF container. It usually stores uncompressed PCM audio, so it is lossless and large, with metadata chunks. It serves for macOS audio production and professional sound editing.

### Programs that open AIFF files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- Audacity brings in AIFF recordings, every PCM variant included, with no extra library.
- VLC media player opens AIFF.
- FFmpeg includes both AIFF encoding and decoding.

**Windows and Mac:**

- Adobe Audition opens uncompressed AIFF and most compressed variants.

**Mac:**

- Apple Music and Logic Pro open it.

### AIFF and M4A compared

An M4A is audio only, stored in the MPEG-4 container. It usually holds AAC, or lossless Apple Lossless (ALAC), and it supports tags and cover art. It is widely supported, and is the usual form for podcasts and music from the Apple stores.

FFmpeg runs in your browser here with `-acodec aac -b:a 192k -vn`, which writes AAC at 192 kbps and drops any video stream. The result is lossy and far smaller than the AIFF. Choose several AIFF files and each is encoded in turn into a separate M4A. No sample rate or channel setting is passed, so there is no control for either. Before you delete the AIFF, play the M4A through once, because AAC discards some detail.

### Other ways to convert AIFF to M4A

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i master.aiff -c:a aac -b:a 192k listening-from-aiff.m4a`.
- **Audacity:** after installing the optional FFmpeg library, open the AIFF, then File > Export Audio and M4A (AAC) Files (FFmpeg). Its AAC export has a quality setting for the bit rate.

### Problems with AIFF files

- **A huge file**: PCM audio takes up space by design, so size alone does not mean damage.
- **Lossless is required**: AAC discards detail, so keep the AIFF as the master.
- **Tracks sound different**: AAC is lossy, so compare the M4A with the AIFF before deleting anything.
- **You need an editable file**: edit the AIFF first and convert last.
- **Metadata**: AIFF carries metadata chunks, so look at the tags in your player after converting.

guide.title: AVI files and M4V output
guide.markdown:
### What is an AVI file?

AVI, Audio Video Interleave, is a RIFF-based container that Microsoft introduced in 1992. It interleaves video with audio and can carry many codecs. It turns up as older Windows video, in camera or capture output, and in archives; modern features are poorly supported.

### Programs that open AVI files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- mpv plays AVI and lets you pick the audio track.
- ffplay plays it.
- Adobe Premiere imports AVI when the decoder is available.

**Mobile:**

- The VLC apps on Android and iOS play AVI on phones.

### AVI and M4V compared

M4V is a video format developed by Apple that is very close to MP4, with H.264 video and AAC audio. HandBrake treats .m4v and .mp4 outputs as the same container. Files from the iTunes Store may carry FairPlay DRM. iTunes and the Apple TV app use it for videos, and so do phones and tablets.

This page runs FFmpeg in your browser. It re-encodes the video as H.264 at CRF 30 with the ultrafast preset and the sound as AAC at 96 kbps, with the index placed first in the file. A filter deinterlaces frames flagged as interlaced, a picture bigger than 1920 px on a side is shrunk to fit, and no more than 30 frames a second are kept. Width and height are then rounded down to even numbers, and a video inside those limits otherwise keeps its size and rate. A batch of AVI files is encoded in turn, one M4V each.

### Other ways to convert AVI to M4V

- **FFmpeg encode:** run `ffmpeg -i archive.avi -c:v libx264 -crf 19 -c:a aac -f mp4 delivery.m4v`. The `-f mp4` picks MP4 packaging for the .m4v name.
- **FFmpeg copy:** run `ffmpeg -i archive.avi -c copy -f mp4 copied.m4v`. The `-c copy` option leaves the streams unchanged instead of re-encoding them.

### Problems with AVI files

- **An old codec**: some players and decoders lack support for older AVI codecs.
- **Sound out of sync**: check the whole clip, not only the opening seconds.
- **Larger than expected**: the page sets no target size, so check the result against your needs.
- **Looks softer than the AVI**: this page trades detail for speed, so use FFmpeg with a lower CRF for archival quality.
